findings.title: Coverage compares different database snapshots
findings.description: Ledger totals and raw counts execute separately on the autocommit connection provided by `store_context.py`. If an ingest commits between these reads, coverage compares the old ledger with new raw rows and falsely reports corruption, exiting 3. Run the comparison in a read-only, repeatable-read transaction and add a concurrent-ingest regression test.

findings.title: An unknown availability edge can report caught up
findings.description: When a tier and start are configured but neither an explicit end nor an observed edge exists, `wanted` becomes `None`. With no held units, the verdict list is empty, yet `caught_up([], wanted=True)` returns `True`. Report an unknown/not-caught-up result rather than claiming completeness without an established range.

findings.title: Coverage repeatedly scans all instrument-session keys on the event loop
findings.description:
Each session reconstructs and scans every ledger and raw key, making report construction quadratic in the session count. This synchronous work runs inside `build_coverage`; an isolated benchmark of the actual function took approximately 0.87 seconds for 500 sessions × 100 instruments. Group counts by session once and offload substantial CPU work; add a coverage-specific load test.

Tests could not run: the available environment lacks `psycopg`, and pytest capture requires temporary-file access unavailable in this read-only sandbox.
